text: But thou, want not! ask not! Find full reward of doing right in right! Let right deeds be thy motive, not the fruit which comes from them.
source: Edwin Arnold, The Song Celestial (1885)

text: The Lord is my shepherd; I shall not want.
source: King James Version

text: Therefore remember Me, I will remember you. Give thanks to Me, and reject not Me.
source: Marmaduke Pickthall, The Meaning of the Glorious Koran (1930)

text: For hatred does not cease by hatred at any time: hatred ceases by love, this is an old rule.
source: F. Max Müller, Sacred Books of the East Vol. X (1881)

text: There is but one God whose name is true, the Creator, devoid of fear and enmity, immortal, unborn, self-existent by the favour of the Guru.
source: Max Arthur Macauliffe, The Sikh Religion (1909), Vol. I

text: Let each man raise the Self by Soul, not trample down his Self, since Soul that is Self's friend may grow Self's foe.
source: Edwin Arnold, The Song Celestial (1885)

text: For God so loved the world, that he gave his only begotten Son, that whosoever believeth in him should not perish, but have everlasting life.
source: King James Version

text: O ye who believe! Seek help in steadfastness and prayer. Lo! Allah is with the steadfast.
source: Marmaduke Pickthall, The Meaning of the Glorious Koran (1930)

text: Not the perversities of others, not their sins of commission or omission, but his own misdeeds and negligences should a sage take notice of.
source: F. Max Müller, Sacred Books of the East Vol. X (1881)

text: How shall man become true before God? How shall the veil of falsehood be rent? By walking, O Nanak, according to the will of the Commander as preordained.
source: Max Arthur Macauliffe, The Sikh Religion (1909), Vol. I

text: But to those blessed ones who worship Me, turning not otherwhere, with minds set fast, I bring assurance of full bliss beyond.
source: Edwin Arnold, The Song Celestial (1885)

text: For I know the thoughts that I think toward you, saith the Lord, thoughts of peace, and not of evil, to give you an expected end.
source: King James Version

text: Allah tasketh not a soul beyond its scope.
source: Marmaduke Pickthall, The Meaning of the Glorious Koran (1930)

text: Rouse thyself! do not be idle! Follow the law of virtue! The virtuous rests in bliss in this world and in the next.
source: F. Max Müller, Sacred Books of the East Vol. X (1881)

text: Nanak, sing His praises who is the Treasury of excellences. Sing and hear and put His love into your hearts. Thus shall your sorrows be removed, and you shall be absorbed in Him who is the abode of happiness.
source: Max Arthur Macauliffe, The Sikh Religion (1909), Vol. I

text: When Righteousness declines, O Bharata! when Wickedness is strong, I rise, from age to age, and take visible shape, and move a man with men, succouring the good, thrusting the evil back, and setting Virtue on her seat again.
source: Edwin Arnold, The Song Celestial (1885)

text: I can do all things through Christ which strengtheneth me.
source: King James Version

text: Say: O My slaves who have been prodigal to their own hurt! Despair not of the mercy of Allah, Who forgiveth all sins. Lo! He is the Forgiving, the Merciful.
source: Marmaduke Pickthall, The Meaning of the Glorious Koran (1930)

text: Not to commit any sin, to do good, and to purify one's mind, that is the teaching of (all) the Awakened.
source: F. Max Müller, Sacred Books of the East Vol. X (1881)

text: Nanak, the saints are ever happy. By hearing the Name sorrow and sin are no more.
source: Max Arthur Macauliffe, The Sikh Religion (1909), Vol. I

text: For wheresoe'er is wondrous work, and majesty, and might, from Me hath all proceeded. Receive thou this aright!
source: Edwin Arnold, The Song Celestial (1885)

text: Trust in the Lord with all thine heart; and lean not unto thine own understanding.
source: King James Version

text: Lo! with hardship goeth ease
source: Marmaduke Pickthall, The Meaning of the Glorious Koran (1930)

text: Health is the greatest of gifts, contentedness the best riches; trust is the best of relationships, Nirvana the highest happiness.
source: F. Max Müller, Sacred Books of the East Vol. X (1881)

text: Nanak, God bestoweth gifts on whom He looketh with favour and mercy.
source: Max Arthur Macauliffe, The Sikh Religion (1909), Vol. I

text: Who hateth nought of all which lives, living himself benign, compassionate, from arrogance exempt, exempt from love of self, unchangeable by good or ill; patient, contented, firm in faith, mastering himself, true to his word, seeking Me, heart and soul; vowed unto Me, that man I love!
source: Edwin Arnold, The Song Celestial (1885)

text: Fear thou not; for I am with thee: be not dismayed; for I am thy God: I will strengthen thee; yea, I will help thee; yea, I will uphold thee with the right hand of my righteousness.
source: King James Version

text: Who have believed and whose hearts have rest in the remembrance of Allah. Verily in the remembrance of Allah do hearts find rest!
source: Marmaduke Pickthall, The Meaning of the Glorious Koran (1930)

text: Let a man overcome anger by love, let him overcome evil by good; let him overcome the greedy by liberality, the liar by truth!
source: F. Max Müller, Sacred Books of the East Vol. X (1881)

ref: Asa ki War, Pauri I (Guru Nanak)
text: O Creator, Thou art the Giver; being pleased Thou bestowest and practisest kindness.
source: Max Arthur Macauliffe, The Sikh Religion (1909), Vol. I

text: And whoso thus discerneth Me in all, and all in Me, I never let him go; nor looseneth he hold upon Me; but, dwell he where he may, whate'er his life, in Me he dwells and lives, because he knows and worships Me, Who dwell in all which lives, and cleaves to Me in all.
source: Edwin Arnold, The Song Celestial (1885)

text: Have not I commanded thee? Be strong and of a good courage; be not afraid, neither be thou dismayed: for the Lord thy God is with thee whithersoever thou goest.
source: King James Version

text: And whosoever putteth his trust in Allah, He will suffice him.
source: Marmaduke Pickthall, The Meaning of the Glorious Koran (1930)

text: Speak the truth, do not yield to anger; give, if thou art asked for little; by these three steps thou wilt go near the gods.
source: F. Max Müller, Sacred Books of the East Vol. X (1881)

ref: Guru Nanak's hymn to the leper (Dhanasari), Life of Guru Nanak
text: Even if he be drowning in sin, God will still take care of him. Nanak, the True One is beneficent to all.
source: Max Arthur Macauliffe, The Sikh Religion (1909), Vol. I

text: Wake! Be thyself! Arise, Scourge of thy Foes!
source: Edwin Arnold, The Song Celestial (1885)

text: God is our refuge and strength, a very present help in trouble.
source: King James Version

text: Thee (alone) we worship; Thee (alone) we ask for help.
source: Marmaduke Pickthall, The Meaning of the Glorious Koran (1930)

text: All that we are is the result of what we have thought: it is founded on our thoughts, it is made up of our thoughts. If a man speaks or acts with a pure thought, happiness follows him, like a shadow that never leaves him.
source: F. Max Müller, Sacred Books of the East Vol. X (1881)

text: By His order souls are infused into them; by His order greatness is obtained.
source: Max Arthur Macauliffe, The Sikh Religion (1909), Vol. I

text: Nor I, nor thou, nor any one of these, Ever was not, nor ever will not be, For ever and for ever afterwards.
source: Edwin Arnold, The Song Celestial (1885)

text: He that dwelleth in the secret place of the most High shall abide under the shadow of the Almighty.
source: King James Version

text: Show us the straight path
source: Marmaduke Pickthall, The Meaning of the Glorious Koran (1930)

text: "He abused me, he beat me, he defeated me, he robbed me,"--in those who do not harbour such thoughts hatred will cease.
source: F. Max Müller, Sacred Books of the East Vol. X (1881)

text: The Giver giveth; the receiver groweth weary of receiving. In every age man subsisteth by His bounty.
source: Max Arthur Macauliffe, The Sikh Religion (1909), Vol. I

text: The soul which is not moved, The soul that with a strong and constant calm Takes sorrow and takes joy indifferently, Lives in the life undying!
source: Edwin Arnold, The Song Celestial (1885)

text: I will lift up mine eyes unto the hills, from whence cometh my help. My help cometh from the LORD, which made heaven and earth.
source: King James Version

text: And when My servants question thee concerning Me, then surely I am nigh. I answer the prayer of the suppliant when he crieth unto Me. So let them hear My call and let them trust in Me, in order that they may be led aright.
source: Marmaduke Pickthall, The Meaning of the Glorious Koran (1930)

text: As rain does not break through a well-thatched house, passion will not break through a well-reflecting mind.
source: F. Max Müller, Sacred Books of the East Vol. X (1881)

text: In describing Him there would never be an end. Millions of men give millions upon millions of descriptions of Him, but they fail to describe Him.
source: Max Arthur Macauliffe, The Sikh Religion (1909), Vol. I

text: Indestructible, Learn thou! the Life is, spreading life through all; It cannot anywhere, by any means, Be anywise diminished, stayed, or changed.
source: Edwin Arnold, The Song Celestial (1885)

text: The LORD is my light and my salvation; whom shall I fear? the LORD is the strength of my life; of whom shall I be afraid?
source: King James Version

text: Spend your wealth for the cause of Allah, and be not cast by your own hands to ruin; and do good. Lo! Allah loveth the beneficent.
source: Marmaduke Pickthall, The Meaning of the Glorious Koran (1930)

text: These wise people, meditative, steady, always possessed of strong powers, attain to Nirvana, the highest happiness.
source: F. Max Müller, Sacred Books of the East Vol. X (1881)

text: Who can sing Him, who is all-seeing and omnipresent?
source: Max Arthur Macauliffe, The Sikh Religion (1909), Vol. I

text: Nay, but as when one layeth His worn-out robes away, And taking new ones, sayeth, 'These will I wear to-day!' So putteth by the spirit Lightly its garb of flesh, And passeth to inherit A residence afresh.
source: Edwin Arnold, The Song Celestial (1885)

text: O taste and see that the LORD is good: blessed is the man that trusteth in him.
source: King James Version

text: Truly Allah loveth those who turn unto Him, and loveth those who have a care for cleanness.
source: Marmaduke Pickthall, The Meaning of the Glorious Koran (1930)

text: By rousing himself, by earnestness, by restraint and control, the wise man may make for himself an island which no flood can overwhelm.
source: F. Max Müller, Sacred Books of the East Vol. X (1881)

text: True is the Lord, true is His name; it is uttered with endless love.
source: Max Arthur Macauliffe, The Sikh Religion (1909), Vol. I

text: Here shall no end be hindered, no hope marred, No loss be feared: faith--yea, a little faith-- Shall save thee from the anguish of thy dread.
source: Edwin Arnold, The Song Celestial (1885)

text: Delight thyself also in the LORD; and he shall give thee the desires of thine heart.
source: King James Version

text: The likeness of those who spend their wealth in Allah's way is as the likeness of a grain which groweth seven ears, in every ear a hundred grains. Allah giveth increase manifold to whom He will. Allah is All-Embracing, All-Knowing.
source: Marmaduke Pickthall, The Meaning of the Glorious Koran (1930)

text: It is good to tame the mind, which is difficult to hold in and flighty, rushing wherever it listeth; a tamed mind brings happiness.
source: F. Max Müller, Sacred Books of the East Vol. X (1881)

text: At the ambrosial hour of morning meditate on the true Name and God's greatness.
source: Max Arthur Macauliffe, The Sikh Religion (1909), Vol. I

text: And like the ocean, day by day receiving Floods from all lands, which never overflows Its boundary-line not leaping, and not leaving, Fed by the rivers, but unswelled by those;-- So is the perfect one! to his soul's ocean The world of sense pours streams of witchery; They leave him as they find, without commotion, Taking their tribute, but remaining sea.
source: Edwin Arnold, The Song Celestial (1885)

text: Cast thy burden upon the LORD, and he shall sustain thee: he shall never suffer the righteous to be moved.
source: King James Version

text: Ye are the best community that hath been raised up for mankind. Ye enjoin right conduct and forbid indecency; and ye believe in Allah.
source: Marmaduke Pickthall, The Meaning of the Glorious Koran (1930)

text: Let the wise man guard his thoughts, for they are difficult to perceive, very artful, and they rush wherever they list: thoughts well guarded bring happiness.
source: F. Max Müller, Sacred Books of the East Vol. X (1881)

text: The Kind One will give us a robe of honour, and by His favour we shall reach the gate of salvation.
source: Max Arthur Macauliffe, The Sikh Religion (1909), Vol. I

text: Work is more excellent than idleness; The body's life proceeds not, lacking work.
source: Edwin Arnold, The Song Celestial (1885)

text: For the LORD is good; his mercy is everlasting; and his truth endureth to all generations.
source: King James Version

text: And vie one with another for forgiveness from your Lord, and for a paradise as wide as are the heavens and the earth, prepared for those who ward off (evil); Those who spend (of that which Allah hath given them) in ease and in adversity, those who control their wrath and are forgiving toward mankind; Allah loveth the good
source: Marmaduke Pickthall, The Meaning of the Glorious Koran (1930)

text: Not a mother, not a father will do so much, nor any other relative; a well-directed mind will do us greater service.
source: F. Max Müller, Sacred Books of the East Vol. X (1881)

text: That there is but one Bestower on all living beings; may I not forget Him!
source: Max Arthur Macauliffe, The Sikh Religion (1909), Vol. I

text: Therefore, thy task prescribed With spirit unattached gladly perform, Since in performance of plain duty man Mounts to his highest bliss.
source: Edwin Arnold, The Song Celestial (1885)

text: The LORD is merciful and gracious, slow to anger, and plenteous in mercy.
source: King James Version

text: Faint not nor grieve, for ye will overcome them if ye are (indeed) believers.
source: Marmaduke Pickthall, The Meaning of the Glorious Koran (1930)

text: As the bee collects nectar and departs without injuring the flower, or its colour or scent, so let a sage dwell in his village.
source: F. Max Müller, Sacred Books of the East Vol. X (1881)

text: Precious stones, jewels, and gems shall be treasured up in thy heart if thou hearken to even one word of the Guru.
source: Max Arthur Macauliffe, The Sikh Religion (1909), Vol. I

text: What the wise choose The unwise people take; what best men do The multitude will follow.
source: Edwin Arnold, The Song Celestial (1885)

text: This is the day which the LORD hath made; we will rejoice and be glad in it.
source: King James Version

text: If Allah is your helper none can overcome you, and if He withdraw His help from you, who is there who can help you after Him ? In Allah let believers put their trust.
source: Marmaduke Pickthall, The Meaning of the Glorious Koran (1930)

text: The scent of flowers does not travel against the wind, nor (that of) sandal-wood, or of Tagara and Mallika flowers; but the odour of good people travels even against the wind; a good man pervades every place.
source: F. Max Müller, Sacred Books of the East Vol. X (1881)

text: If I please Him, that is my place of pilgrimage to bathe in; if I please Him not, what ablutions shall I make?
source: Max Arthur Macauliffe, The Sikh Religion (1909), Vol. I

text: Many there be who come! from fear set free, From anger, from desire; keeping their hearts Fixed upon me--my Faithful--purified By sacred flame of Knowledge. Such as these Mix with my being.
source: Edwin Arnold, The Song Celestial (1885)

text: Thy word is a lamp unto my feet, and a light unto my path.
source: King James Version

text: O ye who believe! Endure, outdo all others in endurance, be ready, and observe your duty to Allah, in order that ye may succeed.
source: Marmaduke Pickthall, The Meaning of the Glorious Koran (1930)

text: If an intelligent man be associated for one minute only with a wise man, he will soon perceive the truth, as the tongue perceives the taste of soup.
source: F. Max Müller, Sacred Books of the East Vol. X (1881)

text: Nanak, God may bestow virtue on those who are devoid of it, as well as on those who already possess it; But no such person is seen as can bestow virtue upon Him.
source: Max Arthur Macauliffe, The Sikh Religion (1909), Vol. I

text: All's then God! The sacrifice is Brahm, the ghee and grain Are Brahm, the fire is Brahm, the flesh it eats Is Brahm, and unto Brahm attaineth he Who, in such office, meditates on Brahm.
source: Edwin Arnold, The Song Celestial (1885)

text: I will praise thee; for I am fearfully and wonderfully made: marvellous are thy works; and that my soul knoweth right well.
source: King James Version

text: Allah would make the burden light for you, for man was created weak.
source: Marmaduke Pickthall, The Meaning of the Glorious Koran (1930)

text: No, that deed is well done of which a man does not repent, and the reward of which he receives gladly and cheerfully.
source: F. Max Müller, Sacred Books of the East Vol. X (1881)

text: By hearing the Name even the low become highly lauded.
source: Max Arthur Macauliffe, The Sikh Religion (1909), Vol. I

text: The sacrifice Which Knowledge pays is better than great gifts Offered by wealth, since gifts' worth--O my Prince! Lies in the mind which gives, the will that serves: And these are gained by reverence, by strong search, By humble heed of those who see the Truth And teach it.
source: Edwin Arnold, The Song Celestial (1885)

text: He healeth the broken in heart, and bindeth up their wounds.
source: King James Version

text: Yet whoso doeth evil or wrongeth his own soul, then seeketh pardon of Allah, will find Allah Forgiving, Merciful.
source: Marmaduke Pickthall, The Meaning of the Glorious Koran (1930)

text: He who drinks in the law lives happily with a serene mind: the sage rejoices always in the law, as preached by the elect (Ariyas).
source: F. Max Müller, Sacred Books of the East Vol. X (1881)

text: By hearing the Name truth, contentment, and divine knowledge are obtained.
source: Max Arthur Macauliffe, The Sikh Religion (1909), Vol. I

text: Believing, he receives it when the soul Masters itself, and cleaves to Truth, and comes-- Possessing knowledge--to the higher peace, The uttermost repose.
source: Edwin Arnold, The Song Celestial (1885)

text: Thou wilt shew me the path of life: in thy presence is fulness of joy; at thy right hand there are pleasures for evermore.
source: King James Version

text: Lo! the mercy of Allah is nigh unto the good.
source: Marmaduke Pickthall, The Meaning of the Glorious Koran (1930)

text: As a solid rock is not shaken by the wind, wise people falter not amidst blame and praise.
source: F. Max Müller, Sacred Books of the East Vol. X (1881)

text: By hearing the Name the mind is composed and fixed on God.
source: Max Arthur Macauliffe, The Sikh Religion (1909), Vol. I

text: He that acts in thought of Brahm, Detaching end from act, with act content, The world of sense can no more stain his soul Than waters mar th' enamelled lotus-leaf.
source: Edwin Arnold, The Song Celestial (1885)

text: Let the words of my mouth, and the meditation of my heart, be acceptable in thy sight, O LORD, my strength, and my redeemer.
source: King James Version

text: Say: Naught befalleth us save that which Allah hath decreed for us. He is our Protecting Friend. In Allah let believers put their trust!
source: Marmaduke Pickthall, The Meaning of the Glorious Koran (1930)

text: His thought is quiet, quiet are his word and deed, when he has obtained freedom by true knowledge, when he has thus become a quiet man.
source: F. Max Müller, Sacred Books of the East Vol. X (1881)

text: Hearing the Name is equal to bathing at the sixty-eight places of pilgrimage.
source: Max Arthur Macauliffe, The Sikh Religion (1909), Vol. I

text: The sage whose soul Holds off from outer contacts, in himself Finds bliss; to Brahma joined by piety, His spirit tastes eternal peace.
source: Edwin Arnold, The Song Celestial (1885)

text: In all thy ways acknowledge him, and he shall direct thy paths.
source: King James Version

text: Go, O my sons, and ascertain concerning Joseph and his brother, and despair not of the Spirit of Allah.
source: Marmaduke Pickthall, The Meaning of the Glorious Koran (1930)

text: Forests are delightful; where the world finds no delight, there the passionless will find delight, for they look not for pleasures.
source: F. Max Müller, Sacred Books of the East Vol. X (1881)

text: By hearing the Name, the depth of the sea of virtue is sounded.
source: Max Arthur Macauliffe, The Sikh Religion (1909), Vol. I

text: Yea! for he knows Me Who am He that heeds The sacrifice and worship, God revealed; And He who heeds not, being Lord of Worlds, Lover of all that lives, God unrevealed, Wherein who will shall find surety and shield!
source: Edwin Arnold, The Song Celestial (1885)

text: Commit thy works unto the LORD, and thy thoughts shall be established.
source: King James Version

text: And whatever of comfort ye enjoy, it is from Allah. Then, when misfortune reacheth you, unto Him ye cry for help.
source: Marmaduke Pickthall, The Meaning of the Glorious Koran (1930)

text: If one man conquer in battle a thousand times thousand men, and if another conquer himself, he is the greatest of conquerors.
source: F. Max Müller, Sacred Books of the East Vol. X (1881)

text: By hearing the Name a blind man findeth his way. By hearing the Name the unfathomable becometh fathomable.
source: Max Arthur Macauliffe, The Sikh Religion (1909), Vol. I

text: Therefore, who doeth work rightful to do, Not seeking gain from work, that man, O Prince! Is Sanyasi and Yogi--both in one And he is neither who lights not the flame Of sacrifice, nor setteth hand to task.
source: Edwin Arnold, The Song Celestial (1885)

text: The name of the LORD is a strong tower: the righteous runneth into it, and is safe.
source: King James Version

text: Whosoever doeth right, whether male or female, and is a believer, him verily we shall quicken with good life, and We shall pay them a recompense in proportion to the best of what they used to do.
source: Marmaduke Pickthall, The Meaning of the Glorious Koran (1930)

text: He who always greets and constantly reveres the aged, four things will increase to him, viz. life, beauty, happiness, power.
source: F. Max Müller, Sacred Books of the East Vol. X (1881)

text: So pure is His name—Whoever obeyeth God knoweth the pleasure of it in his own heart.
source: Max Arthur Macauliffe, The Sikh Religion (1909), Vol. I

text: Let each man raise The Self by Soul, not trample down his Self, Since Soul that is Self's friend may grow Self's foe.
source: Edwin Arnold, The Song Celestial (1885)

text: Thou wilt keep him in perfect peace, whose mind is stayed on thee: because he trusteth in thee.
source: King James Version

text: And say: My Lord! Cause me to come in with a firm incoming and to go out with a firm outgoing. And give me from Thy presence a sustaining Power.
source: Marmaduke Pickthall, The Meaning of the Glorious Koran (1930)

text: If a man does what is good, let him do it again; let him delight in it: happiness is the outcome of good.
source: F. Max Müller, Sacred Books of the East Vol. X (1881)

text: There is no limit to His mercy, and to His gifts there is no limit.
source: Max Arthur Macauliffe, The Sikh Religion (1909), Vol. I

text: That Yojin, so devoted, so controlled, Comes to the peace beyond,--My peace, the peace Of high Nirvana!
source: Edwin Arnold, The Song Celestial (1885)

text: He giveth power to the faint; and to them that have no might he increaseth strength.
source: King James Version

text: And say: Truth hath come and falsehood hath vanished away. Lo! falsehood is ever bound to vanish.
source: Marmaduke Pickthall, The Meaning of the Glorious Koran (1930)

text: Let no man think lightly of good, saying in his heart, It will not come nigh unto me. Even by the falling of water-drops a water-pot is filled; the wise man becomes full of good, even if he gather it little by little.
source: F. Max Müller, Sacred Books of the East Vol. X (1881)

text: By obeying Him man attaineth the gate of salvation.
source: Max Arthur Macauliffe, The Sikh Religion (1909), Vol. I

text: Steadfast a lamp burns sheltered from the wind; Such is the likeness of the Yogi's mind Shut from sense-storms and burning bright to Heaven.
source: Edwin Arnold, The Song Celestial (1885)

text: But they that wait upon the LORD shall renew their strength; they shall mount up with wings as eagles; they shall run, and not be weary; and they shall walk, and not faint.
source: King James Version

text: And lo! verily I am Forgiving toward him who repenteth and believeth and doeth good, and afterward walketh aright.
source: Marmaduke Pickthall, The Meaning of the Glorious Koran (1930)

text: If, like a shattered metal plate (gong), thou utter not, then thou hast reached Nirvana; contention is not known to thee.
source: F. Max Müller, Sacred Books of the East Vol. X (1881)

text: What power and beautiful form are Thine, O God! Who hath power to know how great Thy gifts are?
source: Max Arthur Macauliffe, The Sikh Religion (1909), Vol. I

text: I will declare to thee that utmost lore, Whole and particular, which, when thou knowest, Leaveth no more to know here in this world.
source: Edwin Arnold, The Song Celestial (1885)

text: When thou passest through the waters, I will be with thee; and through the rivers, they shall not overflow thee: when thou walkest through the fire, thou shalt not be burned; neither shall the flame kindle upon thee.
source: King James Version

text: We said: O fire, be coolness and peace for Abraham
source: Marmaduke Pickthall, The Meaning of the Glorious Koran (1930)

text: He who, though dressed in fine apparel, exercises tranquillity, is quiet, subdued, restrained, chaste, and has ceased to find fault with all other beings, he indeed is a Brahmana, an ascetic (sramana), a friar (bhikshu).
source: F. Max Müller, Sacred Books of the East Vol. X (1881)

text: Whatever pleaseth Thee is good. Thou, O Formless One, art ever secure.
source: Max Arthur Macauliffe, The Sikh Religion (1909), Vol. I

text: I am the fresh taste of the water; I The silver of the moon, the gold o' the sun, The word of worship in the Veds, the thrill That passeth in the ether, and the strength Of man's shed seed.
source: Edwin Arnold, The Song Celestial (1885)

text: Call unto me, and I will answer thee, and shew thee great and mighty things, which thou knowest not.
source: King James Version

text: Successful indeed are the believers Who are humble in their prayers
source: Marmaduke Pickthall, The Meaning of the Glorious Koran (1930)

text: If a man hold himself dear, let him watch himself carefully; during one at least out of the three watches a wise man should be watchful.
source: F. Max Müller, Sacred Books of the East Vol. X (1881)

text: So powerless am I, that I cannot even once be a sacrifice unto Thee.
source: Max Arthur Macauliffe, The Sikh Religion (1909), Vol. I

text: All four are good, and seek me; but mine own, The true of heart, the faithful--stayed on me, Taking me as their utmost blessedness, They are not 'mine,' but I--even I myself! At end of many births to Me they come!
source: Edwin Arnold, The Song Celestial (1885)

text: It is of the LORD’S mercies that we are not consumed, because his compassions fail not. They are new every morning: great is thy faithfulness.
source: King James Version

text: The (faithful) slaves of the Beneficent are they who walk upon the earth modestly, and when the foolish ones address them answer: Peace; And who spend the night before their Lord, prostrate and standing
source: Marmaduke Pickthall, The Meaning of the Glorious Koran (1930)

text: Self is the lord of self, who else could be the lord? With self well subdued, a man finds a lord such as few can find.
source: F. Max Müller, Sacred Books of the East Vol. X (1881)

text: Numberless thy worshippers, and numberless Thy lovers.
source: Max Arthur Macauliffe, The Sikh Religion (1909), Vol. I

text: Have Me, then, in thy heart always!
source: Edwin Arnold, The Song Celestial (1885)

text: He hath shewed thee, O man, what is good; and what doth the LORD require of thee, but to do justly, and to love mercy, and to walk humbly with thy God?
source: King James Version

text: Save him who repenteth and believeth and doth righteous work; as for such, Allah will change their evil deeds to good deeds. Allah is ever Forgiving, Merciful. And whosoever repenteth and doeth good, he verily repenteth toward Allah with true repentance
source: Marmaduke Pickthall, The Meaning of the Glorious Koran (1930)

text: He who formerly was reckless and afterwards became sober, brightens up this world, like the moon when freed from clouds.
source: F. Max Müller, Sacred Books of the East Vol. X (1881)

text: Numberless Thy silent worshippers who lovingly fix their thoughts upon Thee.
source: Max Arthur Macauliffe, The Sikh Religion (1909), Vol. I

text: But--higher, deeper, innermost--abides Another Life, not like the life of sense, Escaping sight, unchanging.
source: Edwin Arnold, The Song Celestial (1885)

text: The LORD is good, a strong hold in the day of trouble; and he knoweth them that trust in him.
source: King James Version

text: And when I sicken, then He healeth me, And Who causeth me to die, then giveth me life (again)
source: Marmaduke Pickthall, The Meaning of the Glorious Koran (1930)

text: The uncharitable do not go to the world of the gods; fools only do not praise liberality; a wise man rejoices in liberality, and through it becomes blessed in the other world.
source: F. Max Müller, Sacred Books of the East Vol. X (1881)

text: Numberless Thy names, and numberless Thy places.
source: Max Arthur Macauliffe, The Sikh Religion (1909), Vol. I

text: Richer than holy fruit on Vedas growing, Greater than gifts, better than prayer or fast, Such wisdom is! The Yogi, this way knowing, Comes to the Utmost Perfect Peace at last.
source: Edwin Arnold, The Song Celestial (1885)

text: The LORD thy God in the midst of thee is mighty; he will save, he will rejoice over thee with joy; he will rest in his love, he will joy over thee with singing.
source: King James Version

text: Who persevere, and put their trust in their Lord!
source: Marmaduke Pickthall, The Meaning of the Glorious Koran (1930)

text: Even the gods envy those who are awakened and not forgetful, who are given to meditation, who are wise, and who delight in the repose of retirement (from the world).
source: F. Max Müller, Sacred Books of the East Vol. X (1881)

text: Numberless they who repeat Thy name with all the strength of their intellects.
source: Max Arthur Macauliffe, The Sikh Religion (1909), Vol. I

text: By Me the whole vast Universe of things Is spread abroad;--by Me, the Unmanifest! In Me are all existences contained; Not I in them!
source: Edwin Arnold, The Song Celestial (1885)

text: Be strong and of a good courage, fear not, nor be afraid of them: for the LORD thy God, he it is that doth go with thee; he will not fail thee, nor forsake thee.
source: King James Version

text: As for those who strive in Us, We surely guide them to Our paths, and lo! Allah is with the good.
source: Marmaduke Pickthall, The Meaning of the Glorious Koran (1930)

text: Happy is the arising of the awakened, happy is the teaching of the True Law, happy is peace in the church, happy is the devotion of those who are at peace.
source: F. Max Müller, Sacred Books of the East Vol. X (1881)

text: As great Thy creation, O God, so great is Thy fame. There is no place without Thy name.
source: Max Arthur Macauliffe, The Sikh Religion (1909), Vol. I

text: See! as the shoreless airs Move in the measureless space, but are not space, [And space were space without the moving airs]; So all things are in Me, but are not I.
source: Edwin Arnold, The Song Celestial (1885)

text: Blessed are the peacemakers: for they shall be called the children of God.
source: King James Version

text: And of His signs is this: He created for you helpmeets from yourselves that ye might find rest in them, and He ordained between you love and mercy. Lo! herein indeed are portents for folk who reflect.
source: Marmaduke Pickthall, The Meaning of the Glorious Koran (1930)

text: Let us live happily then, not hating those who hate us! among men who hate us let us dwell free from hatred!
source: F. Max Müller, Sacred Books of the East Vol. X (1881)

text: So when the mind is defiled by sin, It is cleansed by the love of the Name.
source: Max Arthur Macauliffe, The Sikh Religion (1909), Vol. I

text: Whoso shall offer Me in faith and love A leaf, a flower, a fruit, water poured forth, That offering I accept, lovingly made With pious will.
source: Edwin Arnold, The Song Celestial (1885)

text: But seek ye first the kingdom of God, and his righteousness; and all these things shall be added unto you.
source: King James Version

text: He it is Who blesseth you, and His angels (bless you), that He may bring you forth from darkness unto light; and He is ever Merciful to the believers.
source: Marmaduke Pickthall, The Meaning of the Glorious Koran (1930)

text: Let us live happily then, though we call nothing our own! We shall be like the bright gods, feeding on happiness!
source: F. Max Müller, Sacred Books of the East Vol. X (1881)

text: But he who heareth and obeyeth and loveth God in his heart, Shall wash off his impurity in the place of pilgrimage within him.
source: Max Arthur Macauliffe, The Sikh Religion (1909), Vol. I

text: They are in Me, and I in them!
source: Edwin Arnold, The Song Celestial (1885)

text: Come unto me, all ye that labour and are heavy laden, and I will give you rest.
source: King James Version

text: That which Allah openeth unto mankind of mercy none can withhold it; and that which He withholdeth none can release thereafter. He is the Mighty, the Wise.
source: Marmaduke Pickthall, The Meaning of the Glorious Koran (1930)

text: Victory breeds hatred, for the conquered is unhappy. He who has given up both victory and defeat, he, the contented, is happy.
source: F. Max Müller, Sacred Books of the East Vol. X (1881)

text: All virtues are Thine, O Lord; none are mine.
source: Max Arthur Macauliffe, The Sikh Religion (1909), Vol. I

text: And, all for love of them, within their darkened souls I dwell, And, with bright rays of wisdom's lamp, their ignorance dispel.
source: Edwin Arnold, The Song Celestial (1885)

text: But Jesus beheld them, and said unto them, With men this is impossible; but with God all things are possible.
source: King James Version

text: The word from a Merciful Lord (for them) is: Peace!
source: Marmaduke Pickthall, The Meaning of the Glorious Koran (1930)

text: He who possesses virtue and intelligence, who is just, speaks the truth, and does what is his own business, him the world will hold dear.
source: F. Max Müller, Sacred Books of the East Vol. X (1881)

text: Great is the Lord, great is His name; what He doeth cometh to pass.
source: Max Arthur Macauliffe, The Sikh Religion (1909), Vol. I

text: For wheresoe'er is wondrous work, and majesty, and might, From Me hath all proceeded. Receive thou this aright!
source: Edwin Arnold, The Song Celestial (1885)

text: Therefore I say unto you, What things soever ye desire, when ye pray, believe that ye receive them, and ye shall havethem.
source: King James Version

text: For those who do good in this world there is good, and Allah's earth is spacious. Verily the steadfast will be paid their wages without stint.
source: Marmaduke Pickthall, The Meaning of the Glorious Koran (1930)

text: Kinsmen, friends, and lovers salute a man who has been long away, and returns safe from afar.
source: F. Max Müller, Sacred Books of the East Vol. X (1881)

text: Hail! Hail to Him, The primal, the pure, without beginning, the indestructible, the same in every age!
source: Max Arthur Macauliffe, The Sikh Religion (1909), Vol. I

text: Of poets Usana, of saints Vyasa, sage divine; The policy of conquerors, the potency of kings, The great unbroken silence in learning's secret things; The lore of all the learned, the seed of all which springs.
source: Edwin Arnold, The Song Celestial (1885)

text: For with God nothing shall be impossible.
source: King James Version

text: Lo! the promise of Allah is true. And ask forgiveness of thy sin, and hymn the praise of thy Lord at fall of night and in the early hours.
source: Marmaduke Pickthall, The Meaning of the Glorious Koran (1930)

text: He who holds back rising anger like a rolling chariot, him I call a real driver; other people are but holding the reins.
source: F. Max Müller, Sacred Books of the East Vol. X (1881)

ref: Asa ki War, Slok II (Guru Nanak)
text: True Thy praises, true Thy eulogies; True Thy might, O true King.
source: Max Arthur Macauliffe, The Sikh Religion (1909), Vol. I

text: If there should rise Suddenly within the skies Sunburst of a thousand suns Flooding earth with beams undeemed-of, Then might be that Holy One's Majesty and radiance dreamed of!
source: Edwin Arnold, The Song Celestial (1885)

text: Then spake Jesus again unto them, saying, I am the light of the world: he that followeth me shall not walk in darkness, but shall have the light of life.
source: King James Version

text: And your Lord hath said: Pray unto Me and I will hear your prayer.
source: Marmaduke Pickthall, The Meaning of the Glorious Koran (1930)

text: Those who are ever watchful, who study day and night, and who strive after Nirvana, their passions will come to an end.
source: F. Max Müller, Sacred Books of the East Vol. X (1881)

ref: Asa ki War, Slok II (Guru Nanak)
text: Nanak, true are they who meditate on the True One.
source: Max Arthur Macauliffe, The Sikh Religion (1909), Vol. I

text: Who doeth all for Me; who findeth Me In all; adoreth always; loveth all Which I have made, and Me, for Love's sole end That man, Arjuna! unto Me doth wend.
source: Edwin Arnold, The Song Celestial (1885)

text: Peace I leave with you, my peace I give unto you: not as the world giveth, give I unto you. Let not your heart be troubled, neither let it be afraid.
source: King James Version

text: Allah is gracious unto His slaves. He provideth for whom He will. And He is the Strong, the Mighty.
source: Marmaduke Pickthall, The Meaning of the Glorious Koran (1930)

text: Let a wise man blow off the impurities of his self, as a smith blows off the impurities of silver one by one, little by little, and from time to time.
source: F. Max Müller, Sacred Books of the East Vol. X (1881)

ref: Asa ki War, Slok III (Guru Nanak)
text: Wonderful Thy word, wonderful Thy knowledge; Wonderful Thy creatures, wonderful their species.
source: Max Arthur Macauliffe, The Sikh Religion (1909), Vol. I

text: Cling thou to Me! Clasp Me with heart and mind! so shalt thou dwell Surely with Me on high.
source: Edwin Arnold, The Song Celestial (1885)

text: These things I have spoken unto you, that in me ye might have peace. In the world ye shall have tribulation: but be of good cheer; I have overcome the world.
source: King James Version

text: Now whatever ye have been given is but a passing comfort for the life of the world, and that which Allah hath is better and more lasting for those who believe and put their trust in their Lord
source: Marmaduke Pickthall, The Meaning of the Glorious Koran (1930)

text: He in whom that feeling is destroyed, and taken out with the very root, finds rest by day and by night.
source: F. Max Müller, Sacred Books of the East Vol. X (1881)

ref: Asa ki War, Slok III (Guru Nanak)
text: Wonderful to behold Thee present. Beholding these wonderful things I remain wondering.
source: Max Arthur Macauliffe, The Sikh Religion (1909), Vol. I

text: And, if thou canst not worship steadfastly, Work for Me, toil in works pleasing to Me! For he that laboureth right for love of Me Shall finally attain!
source: Edwin Arnold, The Song Celestial (1885)

text: And we know that all things work together for good to them that love God, to them who are the called according to his purpose.
source: King James Version

text: Lo! those who say: Our Lord is Allah, and thereafter walk aright, there shall no fear come upon them neither shall they grieve. Such are rightful owners of the Garden, immortal therein, as a reward for what they used to do.
source: Marmaduke Pickthall, The Meaning of the Glorious Koran (1930)

text: A man is not learned because he talks much; he who is patient, free from hatred and fear, he is called learned.
source: F. Max Müller, Sacred Books of the East Vol. X (1881)

text: Everything existeth by Thy power; Thou art the omnipotent Creator; Thy name is the holiest of the holy. Saith Nanak, Thou beholdest and pervadest all things subject to Thy command: Thou art altogether unrivalled.
source: Max Arthur Macauliffe, The Sikh Religion (1909), Vol. I

text: bring Me thy failure! find Refuge in Me!
source: Edwin Arnold, The Song Celestial (1885)

text: What shall we then say to these things? If God be for us, who can be against us?
source: King James Version

text: We verily created man and We know what his soul whispereth to him, and We are nearer to him than his jugular vein.
source: Marmaduke Pickthall, The Meaning of the Glorious Koran (1930)

text: A man is not an elect (Ariya) because he injures living creatures; because he has pity on all living creatures, therefore is a man called Ariya.
source: F. Max Müller, Sacred Books of the East Vol. X (1881)

ref: Asa ki War, Pauri IV (Guru Nanak)
text: There is no benefactor so great as the true Guru; hear this, all ye people.
source: Max Arthur Macauliffe, The Sikh Religion (1909), Vol. I

text: But most of all I love Those happy ones to whom 'tis life to live In single fervid faith and love unseeing, Drinking the blessed Amrit of my Being!
source: Edwin Arnold, The Song Celestial (1885)

text: Now the God of hope fill you with all joy and peace in believing, that ye may abound in hope, through the power of the Holy Ghost.
source: King James Version

text: So wait patiently (O Muhammad) for thy Lord's decree, for surely thou art in Our sight; and hymn the praise of thy Lord when thou uprisest
source: Marmaduke Pickthall, The Meaning of the Glorious Koran (1930)

text: You yourself must make an effort. The Tathagatas (Buddhas) are only preachers. The thoughtful who enter the way are freed from the bondage of Mara.
source: F. Max Müller, Sacred Books of the East Vol. X (1881)

text: Fearless is the Formless One, whose name is true, And whose creation is the whole world.
source: Max Arthur Macauliffe, The Sikh Religion (1909), Vol. I

text: He is within all beings--and without-- Motionless, yet still moving; not discerned For subtlety of instant presence; close To all, to each; yet measurelessly far!
source: Edwin Arnold, The Song Celestial (1885)

text: Beareth all things, believeth all things, hopeth all things, endureth all things.
source: King James Version

text: Which is it, of the favours of your Lord, that ye deny ?
source: Marmaduke Pickthall, The Meaning of the Glorious Koran (1930)

text: Cut out the love of self, like an autumn lotus, with thy hand! Cherish the road of peace. Nirvana has been shown by Sugata (Buddha).
source: F. Max Müller, Sacred Books of the East Vol. X (1881)

text: Pleasant is the night for those who long for Him in their hearts.
source: Max Arthur Macauliffe, The Sikh Religion (1909), Vol. I

text: Wisdom He is And Wisdom's way, and Guide of all the wise, Planted in every heart.
source: Edwin Arnold, The Song Celestial (1885)

text: And now abideth faith, hope, charity, these three; but the greatest of these is charity.
source: King James Version

text: He is the First and the Last, and the Outward and the Inward; and He is Knower of all things.
source: Marmaduke Pickthall, The Meaning of the Glorious Koran (1930)

text: The disciples of Gotama are always well awake, and their mind day and night always delights in compassion.
source: F. Max Müller, Sacred Books of the East Vol. X (1881)

ref: Asa ki War, Pauri VII (Guru Nanak)
text: Thou art the great Bestower; ever Thou givest gifts which increase a quarterfold.
source: Max Arthur Macauliffe, The Sikh Religion (1909), Vol. I

text: Yet farther will I open unto thee This wisdom of all wisdoms, uttermost, The which possessing, all My saints have passed To perfectness.
source: Edwin Arnold, The Song Celestial (1885)

text: Let all your things be done with charity.
source: King James Version

text: He is Allah, than Whom there is no other God, the Sovereign Lord, the Holy One, Peace, the Keeper of Faith, the Guardian, the Majestic, the Compeller, the Superb. Glorified be Allah from all that they ascribe as partner (unto Him).
source: Marmaduke Pickthall, The Meaning of the Glorious Koran (1930)

text: Good people shine from afar, like the snowy mountains; bad people are not seen, like arrows shot by night.
source: F. Max Müller, Sacred Books of the East Vol. X (1881)

text: He who meeteth the true Guru and fixeth God's name in his heart, obtaineth comfort.
source: Max Arthur Macauliffe, The Sikh Religion (1909), Vol. I

text: And such-- With single, fervent faith adoring Me, Passing beyond the Qualities, conforms To Brahma, and attains Me!
source: Edwin Arnold, The Song Celestial (1885)

text: But the fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace, longsuffering, gentleness, goodness, faith, Meekness, temperance: against such there is no law.
source: King James Version

text: No calamity befalleth save by Allah's leave. And whosoever believeth in Allah, He guideth his heart. And Allah is Knower of all things.
source: Marmaduke Pickthall, The Meaning of the Glorious Koran (1930)

text: An evil deed is better left undone, for a man repents of it afterwards; a good deed is better done, for having done it, one does not repent.
source: F. Max Müller, Sacred Books of the East Vol. X (1881)

ref: Asa ki War, Pauri X (Guru Nanak)
text: Be mine the gift of the dust of the saints' feet: if I obtain it, I shall apply it to my forehead.
source: Max Arthur Macauliffe, The Sikh Religion (1909), Vol. I

text: For I am That whereof Brahma is the likeness! Mine The Amrit is; and Immortality Is mine; and mine perfect Felicity!
source: Edwin Arnold, The Song Celestial (1885)

text: And above all these things put on charity, which is the bond of perfectness.
source: King James Version

text: Let him who hath abundance spend of his abundance, and he whose provision is measured, let him spend of that which Allah hath given him. Allah asketh naught of any soul save that which He hath given it. Allah will vouchsafe, after hardship, ease.
source: Marmaduke Pickthall, The Meaning of the Glorious Koran (1930)

text: They who know what is forbidden as forbidden, and what is not forbidden as not forbidden, such men, embracing the true doctrine, enter the good path.
source: F. Max Müller, Sacred Books of the East Vol. X (1881)

ref: Asa ki War, Slok XII (Guru Nanak)
text: Thou art the true Lord; beautiful is Thy praise; he who uttereth it is saved.
source: Max Arthur Macauliffe, The Sikh Religion (1909), Vol. I

text: Are green and waving hymns which whisper Truth!
source: Edwin Arnold, The Song Celestial (1885)

text: Be careful for nothing; but in every thing by prayer and supplication with thanksgiving let your requests be made known unto God.
source: King James Version

text: And feed with food the needy wretch, the orphan and the prisoner, for love of Him, (Saying): We feed you, for the sake of Allah only. We wish for no reward nor thanks from you
source: Marmaduke Pickthall, The Meaning of the Glorious Koran (1930)

text: Mules are good, if tamed, and noble Sindhu horses, and elephants with large tusks; but he who tames himself is better still.
source: F. Max Müller, Sacred Books of the East Vol. X (1881)

ref: Life of Guru Nanak (boyhood hymn to his schoolmaster)
text: Make divine love thy pen, and thy heart the writer; ask thy guru and write his instruction.
source: Max Arthur Macauliffe, The Sikh Religion (1909), Vol. I

text: Know, too, from Me Shineth the gathered glory of the suns Which lighten all the world: from Me the moons Draw silvery beams, and fire fierce loveliness.
source: Edwin Arnold, The Song Celestial (1885)

text: And the peace of God, which passeth all understanding, shall keep your hearts and minds through Christ Jesus.
source: King James Version

text: He is successful who groweth, And remembereth the name of his Lord, so prayeth
source: Marmaduke Pickthall, The Meaning of the Glorious Koran (1930)

text: This mind of mine went formerly wandering about as it liked, as it listed, as it pleased; but I shall now hold it in thoroughly, as the rider who holds the hook holds in the furious elephant.
source: F. Max Müller, Sacred Books of the East Vol. X (1881)

ref: Life of Guru Nanak (boyhood hymn to his schoolmaster)
text: Write God's name, write His praises, write that He hath neither end nor limit.
source: Max Arthur Macauliffe, The Sikh Religion (1909), Vol. I

text: Now is the sacred, secret Mystery Declared to thee! Who comprehendeth this Hath wisdom! He is quit of works in bliss!
source: Edwin Arnold, The Song Celestial (1885)

text: But my God shall supply all your need according to his riches in glory by Christ Jesus.
source: King James Version

text: But ah! thou soul at peace! Return unto thy Lord, content in His good pleasure!
source: Marmaduke Pickthall, The Meaning of the Glorious Koran (1930)

text: Pleasant is virtue lasting to old age, pleasant is a faith firmly rooted; pleasant is attainment of intelligence, pleasant is avoiding of sins.
source: F. Max Müller, Sacred Books of the East Vol. X (1881)

ref: Life of Guru Nanak (hymn to his mother)
text: O man, obey God and thou shalt be happy.
source: Max Arthur Macauliffe, The Sikh Religion (1909), Vol. I

text: Be thou joyous, Prince! Whose lot is set apart for heavenly Birth.
source: Edwin Arnold, The Song Celestial (1885)

text: Rejoice evermore. Pray without ceasing. In every thing give thanks: for this is the will of God in Christ Jesus concerning you.
source: King James Version

text: He is indeed successful who causeth it to grow
source: Marmaduke Pickthall, The Meaning of the Glorious Koran (1930)

text: The fields are damaged by weeds, mankind is damaged by hatred: therefore a gift bestowed on those who do not hate brings great reward.
source: F. Max Müller, Sacred Books of the East Vol. X (1881)

ref: Life of Guru Nanak (hymn to his mother)
text: Hail, hail to him who showeth the road! Hail, hail to him who communicateth the Word! Hail, hail to him who blendeth us with God!
source: Max Arthur Macauliffe, The Sikh Religion (1909), Vol. I

text: Serenity of soul, benignity, Sway of the silent Spirit, constant stress To sanctify the Nature,--these things make Good rite, and true religiousness of Mind.
source: Edwin Arnold, The Song Celestial (1885)

text: For God hath not given us the spirit of fear; but of power, and of love, and of a sound mind.
source: King James Version

text: Thy Lord hath not forsaken thee nor doth He hate thee, And verily the latter portion will be better for thee than the former, And verily thy Lord will give unto thee so that thou wilt be content.
source: Marmaduke Pickthall, The Meaning of the Glorious Koran (1930)

text: The Bhikshu who acts with kindness, who is calm in the doctrine of Buddha, will reach the quiet place (Nirvana), cessation of natural desires, and happiness.
source: F. Max Müller, Sacred Books of the East Vol. X (1881)

ref: Life of Guru Nanak (the husbandman hymn)
text: Become a husbandman, make good works thy soil, and the word of God thy seed; ever irrigate with the water of truth.
source: Max Arthur Macauliffe, The Sikh Religion (1909), Vol. I

text: The gift lovingly given, when one shall say 'Now must I gladly give!'
source: Edwin Arnold, The Song Celestial (1885)

text: Now faith is the substance of things hoped for, the evidence of things not seen.
source: King James Version

text: Therefor of the bounty of thy Lord be thy discourse.
source: Marmaduke Pickthall, The Meaning of the Glorious Koran (1930)

text: Without knowledge there is no meditation, without meditation there is no knowledge: he who has knowledge and meditation is near unto Nirvana.
source: F. Max Müller, Sacred Books of the East Vol. X (1881)

ref: Life of Guru Nanak (Rag Asa verses)
text: He continueth to give us our daily bread which never faileth.
source: Max Arthur Macauliffe, The Sikh Religion (1909), Vol. I

text: Whoso performeth--diligent, content-- The work allotted him, whate'er it be, Lays hold of perfectness!
source: Edwin Arnold, The Song Celestial (1885)

text: If any of you lack wisdom, let him ask of God, that giveth to all men liberally, and upbraideth not; and it shall be given him.
source: King James Version

text: So when thou art relieved, still toil And strive to please thy Lord.
source: Marmaduke Pickthall, The Meaning of the Glorious Koran (1930)

text: Rouse thyself by thyself, examine thyself by thyself, thus self-protected and attentive wilt thou live happily, O Bhikshu!
source: F. Max Müller, Sacred Books of the East Vol. X (1881)

ref: Life of Guru Nanak (Rag Asa verses)
text: His praise is—that there neither is, Nor was, nor shall be any one like unto Him.
source: Max Arthur Macauliffe, The Sikh Religion (1909), Vol. I

text: And whatsoever deeds he doeth--fixed In Me, as in his refuge--he hath won For ever and for ever by My grace Th' Eternal Rest!
source: Edwin Arnold, The Song Celestial (1885)

text: Casting all your care upon him; for he careth for you.
source: King James Version

text: Read: And thy Lord is the Most Bounteous
source: Marmaduke Pickthall, The Meaning of the Glorious Koran (1930)

text: Him I call indeed a Brahmana who does not offend by body, word, or thought, and is controlled on these three points.
source: F. Max Müller, Sacred Books of the East Vol. X (1881)

ref: Life of Guru Nanak (hymn after the three days)
text: Wherever I look, there art Thou; if I am separated from Thee, I shall burst.
source: Max Arthur Macauliffe, The Sikh Religion (1909), Vol. I

text: So shalt thou come to Me! I promise true, For thou art sweet to Me!
source: Edwin Arnold, The Song Celestial (1885)

text: He that loveth not knoweth not God; for God is love.
source: King James Version

text: Say: He is Allah, the One! Allah, the eternally Besought of all!
source: Marmaduke Pickthall, The Meaning of the Glorious Koran (1930)

text: Him I call indeed a Brahmana who utters true speech, instructive and free from harshness, so that he offend no one.
source: F. Max Müller, Sacred Books of the East Vol. X (1881)
